quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same consonants on both sides. Is the vowel stretched or clipped?
quests.explanation: "Sheep" holds a long, smiling vowel with the tongue high and tense. "Ship" clips it short and lets the mouth go loose.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /iː/ is long and tense with the tongue high and forward; /ɪ/ is short, loose and a little lower and more central. Length and tension travel together, so a stretched vowel usually means /iː/.
quests.mouthPosition: For /iː/ spread the lips as if smiling and lift the tongue high behind the lower teeth. For /ɪ/ let the lips relax and drop the tongue a touch.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to how long the vowel lasts before the /l/ begins.
quests.explanation: It was "fill": a short, relaxed vowel that runs quickly into the /l/. "Feel" would linger on a tense, high vowel first.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Two things separate these vowels: duration and tongue tension. /iː/ is held longer and sounds bright and tight; /ɪ/ is clipped and sounds softer, almost muffled by comparison.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the jaw nearly closed for both, but make /iː/ tighter: lips spread, tongue pushed high and forward. /ɪ/ needs no effort at all - let everything go slack.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Hold a tissue in front of your lips. Would the first sound move it?
quests.explanation: "Pear" opens with a small puff of breath that would flutter a tissue. "Bear" releases the lips with almost no puff and the voice starts at once.
quests.vowelTensionRule: At the start of a word, /p/ is released with a small puff of air (aspiration) and no vocal-fold vibration; /b/ has little or no puff and voicing starts almost immediately.
quests.mouthPosition: Close both lips. For /p/ release them with a clear burst of air; for /b/ release them gently and start the vowel immediately.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Two different verbs. The vowel is the only difference - long or short?
quests.explanation: "Leave" has a long, tense vowel, while "live" has a short, loose one before the same /v/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both vowels are front and high, but /ɪ/ sits slightly lower and more relaxed. The sound your ear catches first is the difference in length: /iː/ lasts noticeably longer.
quests.mouthPosition: Try saying /iː/ with a wide, tense smile, then relax the cheeks and shorten the sound; that slack, quick version is /ɪ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The vowel is wide open in both. Listen to the lips at the very start.
quests.explanation: What you caught was "bark": the lips opened gently with the voice ready to go. "Park" would start with a stronger burst of breath.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are lip stops. The cue is the puff: strong for /p/, weak for /b/. Hold a hand or a tissue in front of your mouth and feel the difference.
quests.mouthPosition: Hold a tissue in front of your lips: it should flutter for /p/ but hardly move for /b/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Neither vowel is long. Listen for how wide the jaw opens.
quests.explanation: "Pen" keeps the jaw half open, so the sound is crisp and narrow. "Pan" drops the jaw and sounds broader.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /e/ is a short mid-front vowel with the jaw only half open; /æ/ is more open and a little longer, with the jaw dropped and the tongue lowered at the front.
quests.mouthPosition: For /e/ open the jaw about halfway and keep the lips relaxed. For /æ/ drop the jaw further and spread the mouth slightly, as if beginning to yawn sideways.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Pay attention to the vowel, since the /m/ and /n/ frame it identically.
quests.explanation: That was "man", the wide, open vowel with the jaw well down. "Men" is a step narrower and more closed.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The difference is jaw opening. /e/ keeps the mouth half open; /æ/ opens it wide so the vowel sounds fuller and broader.
quests.mouthPosition: Start from /e/, then lower the jaw another centimetre without moving the tongue tip from behind the lower teeth - that wide sound is /æ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Start-of-word puff: strong or barely there?
quests.explanation: "Back" begins softly, with the voice ready as soon as the lips part. "Pack" starts with a sharper, breathier release.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The voiceless /p/ releases a burst of breath before the vowel; the voiced /b/ moves quickly into the vowel with the voice already on.
quests.mouthPosition: Press the lips together without tension. Push out air for /p/; let the voice begin for /b/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same start, same end. The vowel decides everything.
quests.explanation: "Chip" is quick and loose, so the word ends fast. "Cheap" stretches the vowel and feels tenser.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /iː/ is long and tense with the tongue high and forward; /ɪ/ is short, loose and a little lower and more central. Length and tension travel together, so a stretched vowel usually means /iː/.
quests.mouthPosition: For /iː/ spread the lips as if smiling and lift the tongue high behind the lower teeth. For /ɪ/ let the lips relax and drop the tongue a touch.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen for the bigger mouth opening in the vowel.
quests.explanation: "Bad" opens wide and lasts a little longer. "Bed" stays at half-open and sounds tighter.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are front vowels, but /æ/ is lower. That extra openness makes /æ/ sound wider and slightly longer than the crisp, short /e/.
quests.mouthPosition: Place a finger under your chin: the jaw should drop noticeably more for /æ/ than for /e/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both round the lips. Which vowel is longer and tighter?
quests.explanation: You heard "pool": the lips pushed forward tightly and the vowel was held. "Pull" is short, and the lips are only loosely rounded.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ʊ/ is short with loosely rounded lips and a tongue that is not quite high; /uː/ is long, with the lips pushed forward into a tight circle and the tongue high at the back.
quests.mouthPosition: For /uː/ push the lips forward into a small, tight round and lift the back of the tongue high. For /ʊ/ keep the lips only loosely rounded and cut the sound short.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The tongue does the same thing in both words. What differs at the release?
quests.explanation: "Die" releases the tongue tip with hardly any breath, and the voice starts quickly. "Tie" adds a clear puff of air.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Initial /t/ is released with a puff of air and no voicing; initial /d/ has little puff and voicing begins almost at once. Aspiration is the audible clue.
quests.mouthPosition: Touch the tongue tip to the ridge behind your upper teeth, then release. Add a puff of air for /t/; let the voice start straight away for /d/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen for a puff of air as the tongue tip lets go.
quests.explanation: "Ten" pops with a breathy release. "Den" glides into the vowel with the voice already on.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both stops are made with the tongue tip on the ridge behind the upper teeth. /t/ adds a burst of breath, /d/ does not.
quests.mouthPosition: A tissue held in front of your mouth should move for /t/ but hardly for /d/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The final cluster is the same. The vowel is the only clue.
quests.explanation: "Send" uses the narrower, half-open vowel. "Sand" widens the mouth and lengthens the vowel slightly.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /e/ is a short mid-front vowel with the jaw only half open; /æ/ is more open and a little longer, with the jaw dropped and the tongue lowered at the front.
quests.mouthPosition: For /e/ open the jaw about halfway and keep the lips relaxed. For /æ/ drop the jaw further and spread the mouth slightly, as if beginning to yawn sideways.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the middle: tight and long, or loose and short?
quests.explanation: "Fool" is held with tightly rounded lips. "Full" is quick, and the lips are softer.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Length and lip tightness separate the two. /uː/ is held longer with a small, firmly rounded mouth, while /ʊ/ is brief and its rounding is soft.
quests.mouthPosition: Say /uː/ as if blowing out a candle, then relax the lips halfway and shorten the vowel - that is /ʊ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both end the same. How wide is the vowel?
quests.explanation: It was "bat": the jaw dropped further and the sound spread. "Bet" would be crisper, with the mouth half open.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The difference is jaw opening. /e/ keeps the mouth half open; /æ/ opens it wide so the vowel sounds fuller and broader.
quests.mouthPosition: Start from /e/, then lower the jaw another centimetre without moving the tongue tip from behind the lower teeth - that wide sound is /æ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same ending. Listen for a long, open vowel or a short, blunt one.
quests.explanation: "March" has a long, open vowel with the jaw dropped wide. "Much" is short and relaxed, with the mouth nearly closed.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ʌ/ is short, central and made with the jaw fairly relaxed; /ɑː/ is long, back and made with the mouth open wide. Duration and openness both help you hear them apart.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɑː/ drop the jaw wide open and let the tongue lie low and back, as if the doctor said 'say ahh'. For /ʌ/ open only a little and keep everything relaxed and short.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both words end on the lips. Listen to how long the vowel is before the closure.
quests.explanation: What you caught was "cab": the vowel lingered slightly and the lips closed softly. "Cap" clips the vowel and shuts sharply.
quests.vowelTensionRule: At the end of a word, the vowel before /b/ is longer than before /p/, and /p/ ends with a crisp stop while /b/ ends softly and may be only partly voiced. Vowel length is the most reliable cue.
quests.mouthPosition: For /p/ close the lips quickly and stop the air. For /b/ hold the vowel longer, then close the lips softly.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: A long open vowel or a short blunt one? Listen before the /k/.
quests.explanation: "Lark" holds a wide-open vowel that seems to come from far back. "Luck" is short and flat.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɑː/ is the longer, deeper vowel with a wide-open mouth; /ʌ/ is a quick, relaxed sound from the middle of the mouth.
quests.mouthPosition: Open wide and hold it for /ɑː/; for /ʌ/ the jaw is barely open and the sound stops almost as soon as it starts.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Focus on the vowel's length and the softness of the ending.
quests.explanation: "Tab" gives the vowel extra time and closes gently. "Tap" is shorter and ends in a crisp stop.
quests.vowelTensionRule: In final position the voiced /b/ lengthens the vowel before it, while /p/ shortens it and closes sharply.
quests.mouthPosition: Stretch the vowel slightly before /b/; cut it off sharply before /p/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The vowel and ending match. Listen for a puff at the start.
quests.explanation: "Goat" begins softly, with the voice starting almost at once. "Coat" begins with a breathy release from the back of the tongue.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Initial /k/ has a strong puff of air and is voiceless; /ɡ/ has very little puff and voicing starts quickly. Both are made at the back of the tongue.
quests.mouthPosition: Raise the back of the tongue to the soft palate. Release with a puff of air for /k/; with a soft, voiced release for /ɡ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Which is the long, open vowel, and which is the short one?
quests.explanation: That was "cut": short, dull and relaxed. "Cart" would stretch the vowel with the jaw wide open.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Listen for a short, blunt vowel (/ʌ/) versus a longer, open one (/ɑː/) that seems to come from further back in the throat.
quests.mouthPosition: The lips stay neutral for both vowels; the real change is the jaw, which drops much further for /ɑː/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same vowel and ending. Feel for a puff of air at the start.
quests.explanation: "Down" starts with the voice on and no puff. "Town" starts with a small burst of breath from the tongue tip.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Voice onset time separates them: /t/ delays it, /d/ starts it immediately.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the tongue tip firm on the ridge for /t/ and a little softer for /d/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both start at the back of the tongue. What differs when it releases?
quests.explanation: The word was "gold": a soft release with the voice starting immediately. "Cold" releases with a breathy puff.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The tongue back touches the soft palate for both; the audible difference is the breathy release of /k/.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the back of the tongue press upward, and hold a tissue in front of the mouth to check the puff for /k/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both start with breath. The vowel decides the meaning.
quests.explanation: "Hut" is a short, flat vowel and finishes quickly. "Heart" opens the jaw and lengthens the vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ʌ/ is short, central and made with the jaw fairly relaxed; /ɑː/ is long, back and made with the mouth open wide. Duration and openness both help you hear them apart.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɑː/ drop the jaw wide open and let the tongue lie low and back, as if the doctor said 'say ahh'. For /ʌ/ open only a little and keep everything relaxed and short.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Short and loose, or long and tense?
quests.explanation: "Seat" has the long, tense vowel with the tongue high. "Sit" has the short, relaxed one.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Two things separate these vowels: duration and tongue tension. /iː/ is held longer and sounds bright and tight; /ɪ/ is clipped and sounds softer, almost muffled by comparison.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the jaw nearly closed for both, but make /iː/ tighter: lips spread, tongue pushed high and forward. /ɪ/ needs no effort at all - let everything go slack.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Only the vowel changes. Which one is held longer?
quests.explanation: You heard "wooed": lips pushed forward and the vowel drawn out. "Wood" is short, with a soft, loose lip shape.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are rounded back vowels. The long one, /uː/, feels tenser and brighter; the short one, /ʊ/, feels loose and comes out quickly.
quests.mouthPosition: Round the lips gently for /ʊ/; for /uː/ tighten and protrude them, and keep the sound going.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The vowel is the same. Listen to how long it lasts before the ending.
quests.explanation: "White" clips the vowel and closes sharply with the tongue tip. "Wide" lets the vowel run longer and ends softly.
quests.vowelTensionRule: At the end of a word, the vowel or sonorant before /d/ lasts longer than before /t/. /t/ is short and sharp; /d/ is longer, softer and partly voiced.
quests.mouthPosition: Touch the tongue tip to the ridge behind the teeth. For /t/ shorten the vowel and stop at once; for /d/ hold the vowel longer and close softly.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the puff of breath at the start of the word.
quests.explanation: "Game" starts softly with the voice on. "Came" starts with a more forceful, breathy release.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /k/ is released with a burst of breath before the vowel; /ɡ/ moves directly into the vowel.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the release gentle for /ɡ/ and let the voice start at once.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the end of the word: sharp stop or soft, voiced one?
quests.explanation: What you caught was "pick", where the vowel is short and the /k/ closes crisply. "Pig" lengthens the vowel and ends softly.
quests.vowelTensionRule: At the end of a word, /ɡ/ lengthens the preceding vowel and is only lightly released; /k/ shortens it and closes with a sharper stop.
quests.mouthPosition: For /k/ shorten the vowel and close the back of the tongue at once. For /ɡ/ hold the vowel longer and close softly.
